sentences.text: Counsel for Applicant(s) :
Shikhar Tandon Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
Mayank Gaurav, G.A. (SL No.206) HON'BLE ANISH KUMAR GUPTA, J. 1.
Heard Sri Shikhar Tandon, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Mayank Gaurav, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Sri Akhilesh Kumar Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The instant application under Section 528 BNSS has been filed seeking quashing of the charge-sheet dated 23.04.2019 as well as impugned cognizance/summoning order dated 07.06.2019 passed in Case No. 21395 of 2019 (State of U.P. vs. Rohit Pal and Ors.) arising out of Case Crime No.
208 of 2018 under Sections 504, 506, 406, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of learned Civil Judge (Junior Division),
FTC-1, Ghaziabad.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that marriage of the applicant no.1 was settled with the opposite party no.2.
Thereafter, the roka, engagement etc., was also done with the consent of both the families.

Thereupon, there are allegations that the applicant no.1 herein called the opposite party no.2 in various hotels and thereafter established physical relationship with her under the garb of said engagement.
Subsequent thereto, due to differences between the parties, the marriage could not be solemnized and subsequently the instant case was lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicant herein.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that after the registration of the F.I.R., the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., where she has categorically stated that the applicant no.1 has never assaulted the opposite party no.2.
Rather, he has agreed to marry the opposite party no.2.

The only allegation is that he has emotionally blackmailed her for establishing the physical relations with the opposite party no.2, on having engaged with the opposite party no.2.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that subsequent to the aforesaid registration of the F.I.R., the matter was investigated and the charge-sheet was filed against the applicants only for the offenses under Section 504, 506, 406, 376 I.P.C. and for rest of the offenses, the applicants herein were exonerated during the investigation itself.
Thereupon, the cognizance was taken against the applicants herein.

During the pendency of the said case, the parties have settled their disputes amicably and a compromise was executed between the parties and the opposite party no.2 has Rohit Pal And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another

On 02.07.2025, the opposite party no.2 herself has given an application along with her affidavit dated 28.06.2025 before the trial court and prayed for not to prosecute the said case against the applicants.

On the basis of the aforesaid settlement, the applicants herein had approach this Court for seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case in view of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
6. Vide order dated 20.08.2025, the Coordinate Bench of this Court has directed the parties to appear before the trial court for verification of compromise.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that as per the direction issued by this Court, the parties had appeared before the trial court on 19.09.2025 in person.

They were properly identified and in presence of both the parties, the parties have admitted the terms and conditions of the compromise, thus the same has been verified by the trial court on 19.09.2025.

A report with regard to the verification of compromise has been received from the Civil Judge, Junior Division, Fast Track Court-I, District Ghaziabad, which is available on record along with the copy of the order dated 19.09.2025 passed by the trial court concerned.
Thus, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceeding on the basis of the aforesaid settlement arrived at between the parties.

7. Learned counsel for the applicants has further stated that though there are allegations with regard to the offense under Section 376 I.P.C., however, on facts of the case, the said allegation is not substantiated as the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.2, both were major, and there was no element of deceit on the part of the applicant since inception of the relationship between the parties.
They were properly engaged, and the opposite party no.2 was a major, educated lady.
Thus, she was fully able to understand the nature of relationship between them.

Thus, whatever relationship were established between the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.1 was the consensual relationship,
thus the offense under Section 376, as alleged in the F.I.R., is not made out.
Thus, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceeding in view of the compromise executed between the parties, which has been duly verified by the trial court.
8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 did not dispute the settlement of dispute between the parties, the execution of compromise and its verification by the trial court.

He further states that the opposite party no.2 do not wish to prosecute the instant case against the applicants herein, thus, he supports the prayer for quashing of the entire proceeding against the applicants herein.

9. Having regard to the nature of dispute between the parties and specifically when the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.2 were major and were fully able to understand the nature of relationship which were consensually established by both of them and finally they have settled their disputes amicably, learned AGA do not oppose the prayer for quashing of the entire proceeding against the applicants.
10. Having heard the rival submissions so made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

From the record of the case, it is apparent that the marriage of the applicant no.1 was settled with the opposite party no.2, Roka, engagement ceremony etc., were also held, and under the garb of such relationship, both the applicant no.1 and the Rohit Pal And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, on the facts of this, no offence under Section 376 I.P.C is made out against the applicant no.1.

Otherwise also, the parties have settled their disputes amicably and they have proceeded ahead in their life as they are married to separate persons out of their free will and choice, and pendency of the instant case would hamper the life of the opposite party no.2 as well. 11.

In view thereof, and having regard to the settlement of dispute amicably, this Court has found it appropriate to quash the proceeding of the instant case in the light of the judgments Gian Singh vs.
State of Punjab and Another : (2012) 10 SCC 303; Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another : (2017) 9 SCC 641; Narinder Singh & Ors. vs.
State of Punjab : (2014) 6 SCC 466 and B.S.Joshi and Other vs. State of Haryana and Another :
(2003) 4 SCC 67, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings in Case No. 21395 of 2019 (State of U.P. vs. Rohit Pal and Ors.) arising out of Case Crime No. 208 of 2018 under Sections 504, 506, 406, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of learned Civil Judge (Junior Division), FTC-1, Ghaziabad, are hereby quashed.
